title: Gunship
build: original disk, Rapidlok V6, PAL, C64 Preservation Project gunship_s1/s2[microprose_1985](rl6)(pal)

records.c: The roster check the boot program calls (SYS 28672) after reading the roster from track 1: $A5 = 0 if it is good, 1 if not. Eleven 64-byte records, numbers 0 to 11 less 8, must each have a 20-byte name of capitals, digits and punctuation (bytes below $60) or shifted letters ($C1-$DA), and bytes 20 to 46 each no higher than their limits at $706F; the first byte of record 8, the pilot chosen last, must be below 8 or 11.
Checks record X: its name, then bytes 46 down to 20 against their limits.
The roster is corrupted: $A5 = 1.
The low bytes of the twelve 64-byte records' addresses, $8C40 to $8FC0 (record 8, $8EC0, is not a pilot).
The limits' table counted from 20 bytes before it, so that byte Y of a record is checked against $705B+Y; the limits themselves start at $706F.
The high bytes of the records' addresses, $8C to $8F.

The highest value each of a record's bytes 20 to 46 may hold: the rank 7; the score and the first decoration 255; the next five 1; the other seven decorations 255; four bytes 3; the three choices of how real the flying is 1, then 2, 4 and 2; and the pilot's fate 2.

Fills the button tables: the next byte is the number of buttons less 1, then each table's values in turn, $7818 tables of 24 from $7591.

Reads the next byte of the script.

The next character: PETSCII to the font's order ($40-$5F less $40, $C0-$DF less $80), then its glyph at $C000 plus 8 times that.

Reads the joystick in port 2 each frame and moves the pointer one step in each direction pushed. Held, the steps come faster: the wait between them halves each time, from 8 frames down to none. The pointer stays inside its box ($7728-$772B), and sprite 0 is put at it: x plus 12, times 2; y times 2, plus 50.
Waits for the interrupt to count a frame ($F7).

Lights or puts out button X, the same EOR doing both: its colour into its rectangle's cells (7F8A), and its second rectangle's too, inverting the rows around them when bit 7 of $7609 says so.
EORs colour A into a box from row Y, column X, $7FE4+1 rows by $7FE3+1 columns: the high nybble into the bytes of the screen at page $A6, the low nybble into colour RAM.
The ADC at $7F94: the box's column, added to the row's address.

KE+81: unpacks a picture (8678) and leaves its colours at $9800 and $9C00.
Five bytes before the cartridge signature that nothing in the library reads.

A cartridge's signature: two vectors, both $8009, and CBM80 with bit 7 set on its letters. With it in memory the KERNAL's reset routine jumps to $8009 instead of starting BASIC. Its RESTORE handler would too, but the boot program points the NMI vector at an RTI in the KERNAL (POKE 792,193).
Where a reset lands: blanks the screen and loops for ever.

KE+0: waits for the fire button with the pointer on a button, and returns the button's number in $A5. A button that is lit already is ignored. A choice puts out the lit one of its group, lights, and returns at once. A plain button lights while the fire button is held and returns when it is let go; moved off while held, it goes out and the wait starts again. One with bit 6 returns every 20 frames while held, put out each time.
The pointer is on button X.
A plain button is held: waits for the fire button to be let go, or for the repeat count to run out.
While the fire button is held: is the pointer still on the button?

Installs the interrupt routine at A (low byte) and X (high) in the KERNAL's vector at $0314, with the raster interrupt at line 0, the band counter $F8 and list position $FA at 0, and only sprite 0's x high bit kept; waits for line 250.

KE+36: unpacks the picture whose header is at $97FB, SMALL's format: first moves the packed bytes up to end at $BFFF, then unpacks them from its start address up to $BFFF. The next packed byte: anything but the escape byte is itself; the escape is followed by a value and a count, and the value is written 4 plus count times, a count of 255 adding another count.

KE+57: draws the theatre map on the text screen at $C800. The map is 16 by 16 squares, of which rows and columns 2 to 13 are drawn, each square three characters wide and two high: their codes run from $3A plus six times the square's terrain ($9200), with colours from $9100. Then units $79 down to 6, from $9400 (x), $9480 (y) and $9600 (state): one whose state has bit 7, 6 or 4 set is drawn as character $20 plus the state's low four bits, coloured by its state ($772C-$772F).
Writes three characters of the map, numbered from X, and their colours from $9100.
KE+78: copies with $01 = $20, every ROM and the I/O out.

The roster as the boot program read it from side 1, track 1, sectors 1 to 4, 256 bytes each. This 1 KB is shared: a picture's screen colours go here, and KE+15 saves colour RAM here, so the front end keeps the roster in RS$() while it runs and puts it back to save it. Each sector starts with 64 bytes that are not a record: two bytes linking to the next sector (track 1 and the sector, which the front end writes before saving) and 62 that nothing reads.

Records 0 to 2, 64 bytes each, laid out as the front end reads them: 0-19 the name; 20 the rank, 0 to 7 for SGT, WO1, 2LT, 1LT, CPT, MAJ, LTC and COL; 21-22 the score, shown times 10; 23-35 how many of each of 13 decorations the pilot holds, SR, NDS, SEAC, CAC, MEC, WEC, AM, PH, ACM, BSV, SS, DSC and CMOH as the front end abbreviates them; 36-39 four values up to 3, not decoded; 40-42 the three choices of how real the flying is (flight, landings, weather); 43-45 three more of the pilot's settings, not decoded; 46 the pilot's fate: 0, or 1 killed in action, or 2 missing in action.
The second sector's first 64 bytes: its link and 62 bytes nothing reads.
Records 3 to 5, laid out as at $8C40.
The third sector's first 64 bytes: its link and 62 bytes nothing reads.
Records 6 and 7, the last of the eight pilots the roster screen lists.
Record 8 is not a pilot: its first byte is the number of the pilot chosen last, 0 to 7, or 11 for none, which the front end puts here before saving. The rest is not read.
The fourth sector's first 64 bytes: its link and 62 bytes nothing reads.
Records 9 and 10, laid out as at $8C40, checked like the others; the roster screen does not list them.
Record 11, which holds the name Kilroy; the boot program writes it, with 11 in record 8, when it clears a corrupted roster.

Five bytes in the form of the unpacker's header (8678): the escape byte $23, the start $9800 and the end $A767. The bytes they describe are not a packed picture (2 KB of zeros, then the sprite shapes), and what the header was left from is not known.
The header's start address, low byte; the unpacker writes from here.
The start address, high byte.
The header's end address: the last packed byte, low byte.
The end address, high byte.
2 KB of zeros where an unpacked picture's colours go: $9800-$9BFF its screen colours, which KE+36 copies to $8C00 a page at a time.
The second page of the screen colours.
The third page.
The fourth page.
$9C00-$9FFF: an unpacked picture's colour RAM values, which KE+36 copies into colour RAM a page at a time.
Their second page.
Their third page.
Their fourth page.

The front end's sprite shapes, 64 bytes each, $80 to $E6 as the VIC numbers them in bank 3: the boot program copies $A000-$BF3F to $E000 (line 480), where the VIC finds them; pictures are unpacked over $A000 later. Shapes $80-$8F: the upper halves of large badges, each built from several shapes.
Shapes $90-$9F: the lower halves of the badges, and pieces of faces.
Shapes $A0-$AF: faces, each built from two or three shapes.
Shapes $B0-$BF: the pointer's arrow ($B1), and more pieces of faces and emblems.
Shapes $C0-$CF: striped ribbons, slashes, a palm tree and the side views of weapons.
Shapes $D0-$DF: a helicopter seen from the front, missiles and rockets with their flames, wrenches and a soldier.
Shapes $E0-$E6: bars, blocks and a cross; zeros follow from $B9C0.
Zeros to $BFFF; the boot program's copy stops at $BF3F.
The front end's character set, which the VIC reads from $C000 in bank 3: 128 characters, lower and upper case.
Characters 128 to 255, which the KERNAL prints for reversed text: most are the first 128 reversed, but 23 ($00, $06, $3C, $3E and $61-$74) are other shapes, not decoded.
